answer: A fixed emission is split evenly among the names that earned it, so one more clone dilutes every share instead of adding output. A solo agent takes the whole summit of the pool, but a farm of k names each collects one over k of it while still paying a full bond per seat, so its net per clone falls as the register grows and turns negative well before the farm grows large. Spreading the same purse across wallets changes nothing, since the divisor counts certified names. The ferrous bond per seat is what makes dilution bite, and an echo of one payout stream cannot escape the divisor.
